Best apps to transcribe voice memos on iPhone (2026)

Start with the app you already have: on iPhone 12 or later, Apple’s Voice Memos transcribes recordings in English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German and a few other languages, and Apple Intelligence can summarize the transcript on newer models. Another app helps when you want imported or very long recordings handled the same way, a summary shaped for a lecture or a meeting, more languages, or the same app on Android. This page compares nine options using only what each vendor states on its own pages, checked on October 26, 2026.

Can iPhone transcribe voice memos without another app?

Yes, on iPhone 12 or later. Apple’s iPhone User Guide (iOS 27) says Voice Memos transcribes speech in English (all variants), Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, French, German, Japanese, Korean and Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), and that the feature isn’t available in every country or region. You can watch the transcript while you record, copy it afterwards with Copy Transcript, and search across titles and transcripts. With Apple Intelligence, Writing Tools can summarize a transcript; on iOS 27 that needs an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or an iPhone 16 or later.

The Notes app does the same inside a note: tap Record Audio, and according to Apple’s Notes guide the spoken words are transcribed when the device language is one of those languages, with an Apple Intelligence summary on supported models. If your recordings are in one of these languages and you mainly want to read or copy what was said, the built-in apps may be all you need.

Otter

Otter (Otter.ai, Inc.) has apps for iPhone and Android, a web app and a desktop app for Mac and Windows. It records and transcribes live, imports audio and video files and writes automatic meeting summaries. Its help center lists English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Chinese (Simplified) as supported languages and marks German and Chinese as beta.

A good fit if you work in English or another language on its list and want the same notes on your phone, in the browser and on your computer.

Notta

Notta runs on iPhone and Android, on the web and as a desktop app for Windows and macOS (supported environments). The app’s home screen offers Import Files, Record Now and Live Transcribe Meetings, its language list is long and includes English, Spanish and Portuguese, and its App Store listing describes AI summaries.

A good fit if you switch between phone and computer and record in several languages.

Transkriptor

Transkriptor is available for iOS and Android, on the web, as a Chrome extension and as a desktop app for Windows and Mac. Its App Store listing describes an integrated audio recorder, voice memo and file transcription (MP3, WAV, M4A), AI summaries and a chat with the transcript, and its website names English, Spanish and Portuguese among many languages.

A good fit if you also want a browser extension or a desktop recorder for online meetings.

Transcribe – Speech to Text (DENIVIP)

Transcribe – Speech to Text (DENIVIP Group OOO, App Store id1241342461) works on iPhone, iPad and Mac and in a web editor at transcribe.com. Its App Store listing describes a built-in voice recorder with live transcription, audio and video uploads, speaker separation, and AI summaries and key points, and its help center names English, Spanish and Portuguese among many languages. Other apps have similar names, so check the developer before you download.

A good fit if you work on an iPhone and a Mac and also want to edit transcripts in a browser.

Aiko

Aiko, from the independent developer Sindre Sorhus, turns recordings of meetings, lectures and voice memos into text with OpenAI’s Whisper model running on the device; the developer says the audio is never uploaded. It runs on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Vision Pro, and its App Store listing requires iOS 26 or later and an A12 Bionic chip or newer.

A good fit if you want the transcription to stay on your device.

TurboScribe

TurboScribe is a web app. Its help page says there is no TurboScribe app in the App Store or on Google Play and that the website works fully in a phone’s browser, including uploads, transcription, translation and export. You can upload a voice memo or record with the microphone in the browser, its audio languages include English, Spanish and Portuguese, and TurboScribe GPT summarizes transcripts through ChatGPT.

A good fit if you mostly upload files, often from a computer, and don’t need an app.

Verbi

Verbi is an AI voice recorder and note taker for iPhone and Android. It records in the app (Pro has no length limit, and on iPhone the recording keeps going with the screen locked), imports files, and takes voice memos, WhatsApp and Telegram voice messages and other audio shared from any app, as well as video links. It transcribes 39 languages and can detect the language for you.

Summaries come from nine templates, such as Lesson Notes, General Meeting and Action Items, and contain only what was said: owners and due dates appear only when someone stated them. With Pro, every transcript gets a summary, and you can tell the speakers apart, chat with the transcript, translate it and export it as TXT or PDF; on the free plan, your first summary is on us and you can copy the text. Verbi needs no account, and recordings and transcripts are stored on your phone. To transcribe, the audio is sent to our speech-to-text providers (ElevenLabs and OpenAI), as the privacy policy explains. The free plan includes 60 minutes of transcription a month.

A good fit if you record long lectures, meetings or interviews, work in more than one language or on both iPhone and Android, and want a summary shaped for the recording. Verbi has no web or desktop version.

How do I choose a voice memo transcription app?

It depends on what you record and what you want from the text. Going by the table:

  • Lectures you want as study notes: you need recording and a summary. Voice Memos and Notes summarize with Apple Intelligence on supported iPhones; Otter, Notta, Transkriptor, Transcribe and Verbi write AI summaries, and Verbi’s Lesson Notes template keeps to what the lecturer said. See how to record a lecture and get study notes.
  • A recorder that transcribes and summarizes: Apple (with Apple Intelligence), Otter, Notta, Transkriptor, Transcribe, TurboScribe (through ChatGPT) and Verbi all list AI summaries. Compare where you record (phone, browser or computer) and which languages you need.
  • Free transcription on iPhone: Voice Memos and Notes are already on your iPhone 12 or later. Other apps’ plans change often, so we don’t list them here; Verbi’s free plan includes 60 minutes of transcription a month.
  • Audio that shouldn’t leave the phone: Aiko transcribes on the device. For any other app, read its privacy page; Verbi sends the audio to its speech-to-text providers to transcribe it.
  • Android as well: Otter, Notta, Transkriptor and Verbi have Android apps, and TurboScribe works in any browser.
  • Working at a computer: Otter, Notta and Transkriptor have desktop apps, Transcribe has a Mac app and a web editor, and TurboScribe is web-based.
  • A language that isn’t on Apple’s or Otter’s list: check the vendor’s own list. Verbi transcribes 39 languages, among them Turkish, Arabic, Hindi and Indonesian.

How do I transcribe a voice memo with Verbi?

  1. Download Verbi from the App Store and open it. In Settings → Transcription Language, pick the language of the recording, or leave it on Auto-detect.
  2. In Voice Memos, tap the recording and open the share sheet.
  3. Choose Verbi. “Added to Verbi. Open the app to transcribe it.” means the recording was handed over. Share it in the default format: Apple’s export page says Options → Editable exports QuickTime Audio, a format Verbi doesn’t read.
  4. Open Verbi. The recording is imported and transcribed; with Pro, you first choose the Number of Speakers. On iOS 26 or later, a long transcription keeps going if you leave the app, and Verbi sends a notification when it’s done; on older iOS versions, it continues when you reopen Verbi.
  5. Read, search or copy the text; with Pro, export it as TXT or PDF. A memo saved in Files can also be picked with Upload File. More in how to transcribe an audio file or voice memo.

Frequently asked questions

Can iPhone transcribe voice memos without an app?

Yes, on iPhone 12 or later. Apple’s iPhone User Guide (iOS 27) says Voice Memos transcribes English, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, French, German, Japanese, Korean and Chinese, and that the feature isn’t available in every country or region (checked October 26, 2026). Open the recording, tap the More button and choose Copy Transcript.

What’s a free app to transcribe voice memos on iPhone?

If your recordings are in one of Apple’s transcription languages, Voice Memos itself is free and already installed. Other apps’ plans change often, so this page doesn’t list them; check each app’s own page. Verbi is free to download, and its free plan includes 60 minutes of transcription a month, recordings kept for 15 days and your first AI summary.

Which app transcribes and summarizes voice recordings?

According to their own pages, Otter, Notta, Transkriptor, Transcribe (DENIVIP) and Verbi write AI summaries; Apple’s Voice Memos and Notes summarize with Apple Intelligence on supported iPhones, and TurboScribe through ChatGPT. Verbi’s summaries come from nine templates and keep to what was said.

Is Whisper an app?

No. Whisper is OpenAI’s open-source speech recognition model, not an iPhone app on its own. Apps build on it: Aiko, for example, runs Whisper on the device.

Can I transcribe voice memos on Android?

Voice Memos is an Apple app, but Verbi, Otter, Notta and Transkriptor also have Android apps. On Pixel phones, Google’s Recorder app transcribes English and several other languages as you record.
